title: How decision records work: record, trace, verify, drift

subject.lede: A decision record is a note pinned to the code it explains, with a smoke alarm attached. The note says what was chosen, what lost and why. The alarm is each assumption's own shell command, which fails the day that assumption stops being true. The pin is a list of file patterns, so anyone about to change a file can ask which decisions govern it, and the ledger can say which decisions had their code change underneath them. In 100x this is the decide command (new, lint, trace, verify, drift, index), and the decision-records skill says when to use it. One level down from the 100x-plugin overview page.

tldr.what: Keeps the reason behind each non-obvious choice next to the code it governs, so a later change can find it and ask whether it still holds.
tldr.how: Each record lists its options, the deciding factor, assumptions that each carry a check command, and the file patterns it governs; trace, verify and drift read those.
tldr.watch_out: Drift says all clear when the commit a record names no longer exists, as after a squash merge, so a silent drift is not proof.

context.purpose: When you or an agent picks one approach over another, this records why, in a file the code can be traced back to; months later, before changing that code, one command says which decision governs it and whether its assumptions still hold.
context.why_now: An agent makes dozens of silent choices per feature, none of them visible in the diff; a month later nobody can say why the code is the way it is, or whether the reason still holds.
in_scope: Writing a record: decide new, and lint, which refuses a record that only names the winner
Assumptions that carry their own check command, and verify, which runs them
Trace: which decisions govern a file
Drift: which decisions had their governed files change since they were recorded
Every decide function, in the Code reference
out_of_scope: Searching the whole ledger of PRDs, specs, RCAs and reviews (ledger find, gaps, and sharding past {{shard_n}})
Whether a code change contradicts a decision: drift only knows that governed files changed

entry_points.label: decide index | check

terms.means: One file per choice, numbered in order with an ADR prefix, with a machine-readable meta block on top and the written reasoning below.
terms.example: The record that keeps gh inside the pr-review skill's steps, in this repo's decisions folder.

terms.means: The fenced JSON at the top of a record that the tools read: id, status, date, options, assumptions, the file patterns it governs and the commit it was written at.
One approach that was considered, with its fit and either why it won or why it did not.
A pass or fail filter applied before any scoring: an option that does not solve the problem is out, whatever it would score.
Something that must stay true for the decision to stay right, written as a claim, a check command and a revisit trigger.
A shell command that fails the day its assumption stops being true.
terms.example: ! grep -rq jwt src/auth  (fails once the session code mentions a token library)

terms.means: The observable event that should make someone re-read the decision.
terms.example: a mobile client needs offline sign-in

terms.means: The file patterns a decision governs. Trace and drift read them.
Asking which recorded decisions govern a given file, before you change it.
A decision whose governed files changed in a commit made after the one the record was written at.
Replacing an accepted record with a new one that names it, instead of editing the old one in place.
The table of what a decision deliberately does not handle; lint warns when it is empty.

outline.title: cmd_drift(): which decisions had their code move

lines.code: for r in load_all(): skip superseded and rejected
rc, out, _ = git diff --name-only {commit}..HEAD -- affects   # rc never read
if changed: DRIFT, print changed[:6], 're-read ... supersede it'

outline.title: cmd_trace(path): which decisions govern a file

lines.code: for r in load_all(): for pat in r.affects:
if fnmatch(path, pat) or path.startswith(pat.rstrip('*/')): hit
if no hits: print 'no recorded decision governs <path>'; return 0
for r in hits: print id, [status], title, each assumption's claim

outline.title: cmd_verify(): run every assumption's own check

lines.code: for r in load_all(), skipping superseded and rejected:
if no command, or a <placeholder>: SKIP unverifiable
rc = bash -c asm.verify   # not a login shell
if rc != 0: FAIL, print the command, its exit status, revisit_when
return 1 if failed else 0   # a skip never fails

diagrams.title: What a decision record is made of
diagrams.source:
mindmap
  %% level: 2
  root((decision records))
    Record
      decide new
      lint
      index
    Assumption
      claim
      verify command
      revisit_when
    Found from the code
      affects patterns
      trace
    Still true?
      verify
      drift
diagrams.caption: Read outward from the centre: how a record is written, what an assumption carries, how a file finds its record, and how the ledger checks a record still holds.

diagrams.title: Before a change: trace, verify, drift
diagrams.source:
sequenceDiagram
  %% level: 2
  actor Dev as You or an agent
  participant Decide as decide command
  participant Records as Decision records
  participant Shell
  participant Git as Code and git history
  Dev->>Decide: trace src/auth/session.ts
  Decide->>Records: match the path against each affects pattern
  Records-->>Decide: ADR-0001 and its assumptions
  Decide-->>Dev: decisions governing the file
  Dev->>Decide: verify
  Decide->>Shell: bash -c each assumption's check
  Shell-->>Decide: exit status
  Decide-->>Dev: ok, or FAIL with revisit_when
  Dev->>Decide: drift
  Decide->>Git: git diff --name-only commit..HEAD -- affects
  alt governed files changed
    Git-->>Decide: changed paths
    Decide-->>Dev: DRIFT, re-read the record
  else nothing changed, or the commit is unknown
    Git-->>Decide: empty output
    Decide-->>Dev: nothing needs attention
  end
diagrams.caption: Trace finds the record; verify asks whether its assumptions still hold right now; drift asks whether its files moved in later commits. The else branch is where an unknown commit hides.

diagrams.title: A record's lifecycle
diagrams.source:
stateDiagram-v2
  [*] --> proposed: decide new
  proposed --> accepted: options and assumptions filled, lint clean
  proposed --> rejected
  accepted --> revisit: drift or a failed verify
  revisit --> accepted: re-read, still holds
  revisit --> superseded: a new record replaces it
  accepted --> superseded: a new record replaces it
  superseded --> [*]
  rejected --> [*]
diagrams.caption: The states are the statuses lint accepts. Verify and drift stop checking a record once it is superseded or rejected.

diagrams.title: How trace decides a pattern matches a path
diagrams.source:
flowchart TD
  %% level: 2
  P[the path, exactly as typed] --> F{"fnmatch(path, pattern)?"}
  F -- yes --> H[the decision governs the path]
  F -- no --> S{"path starts with the pattern minus its trailing * and /?"}
  S -- yes --> H
  S -- no --> N[next pattern; none left: no recorded decision]
diagrams.caption: Both tests compare text. A leading ./ or an absolute path fails both, and the prefix test lets a folder that merely starts with the same letters match.

sk-verify.anchor: shell command that fails when it stops being true

sk-rule1.anchor: Record a decision when the choice was not forced

sk-rule4.anchor: Never edit an accepted decision in place

dd-no-rc.absent: any test of git diff's exit status in drift: the only exit-status test in the file is verify's

scenarios.title: Record a choice, trace it, and catch the day its assumption breaks

steps.t: You chose server sessions over tokens, so the skill says record it now
steps.d: The choice was not forced and is not trivially reversible, and the reasoning evaporates within days.

steps.t: Decide new writes a numbered record, pinned to the current commit
steps.d: The id is the next free number across the folder and its shards. The meta block records the current commit, which drift will later diff from; then the index is rewritten.
code: did = next_id()   # max ADR number in the folder and its shards, plus one
meta = {id, title, status: proposed, affects, commit: git rev-parse --short HEAD, ...}

steps.t: Lint refuses the untouched template with {{tmpl_errs}}
steps.d: No option has a real fit, the winner has no reason, the loser no reason it lost, and the assumption has neither a claim nor a revisit trigger.
do: {{tmpl_errs}}: no fit, no why or why not, no claim, no revisit trigger

steps.t: You fill it: two options with fit and a reason each, and one assumption with its check
steps.d: A record that names only the winner cannot be re-evaluated, which is the only reason to keep it.
code: options: JWT (fit pass, why_not: cannot revoke), server session (fit pass, chosen, why: revocable)
A1.claim: sessions are stored server-side, never in a JWT
A1.revisit_when: a mobile client needs offline sign-in

steps.t: Lint passes; an empty gaps table would only have warned
Before editing the session file, trace says which decision governs it
steps.d: It matches the path against every record's affects patterns and prints each hit's id, status, title and assumptions.

steps.t: Someone adds a token library to the session file, not yet committed
Verify runs each assumption's own check, and this one fails at once
steps.d: It prints the claim, the command, its exit status and the revisit trigger. The check runs in a plain shell, not a login one, so profile noise is never reported as the failure.
do: FAIL on A1, revisit_when: a mobile client needs offline sign-in

steps.t: Drift is still silent: it compares commits, not your working files
steps.d: It diffs from the record's commit to the last commit, so an edit nobody has committed is invisible to it.

steps.t: After the commit, drift names the decision and the file that moved
steps.d: It lists up to {{shown_n}} changed files per record and says to re-read it, then supersede it if it no longer matches. Path-level only: it cannot tell whether the change contradicts the decision.
do: DRIFT on Session strategy: one file changed under src/auth/**

steps.t: A new record supersedes the old one, which is never edited in place

scenarios.title: Drift says all clear when the record's commit no longer exists

steps.t: The branch is squash-merged, so the commit the record names never reaches the main line
steps.d: The record was written on the feature branch. After a squash merge or a rebase, a fresh clone has no commit with that id.

steps.t: Drift's diff fails on the unknown commit, and the failure is thrown away
steps.d: The command's exit status is read into a variable nothing checks; the empty output reads as no changed files.

steps.t: Drift reports nothing to attend to, and exits clean
steps.d: Reproduced in a scratch repo by setting a record's commit to an id that does not exist: no drift line, success exit, while git itself exits with an error.

steps.t: Verify still catches the broken assumption, because it runs the check itself
steps.d: This is why the skill pairs the two before shipping: drift asks whether files moved, verify asks whether the claim still holds.

scenarios.title: Trace compares paths as text, so it can miss a decision or invent one

steps.t: Trace for a path written with a leading ./ finds nothing
steps.d: Measured in this repo: the work file is governed by three records, but asked as ./scripts/work.py trace says no decision governs it, and calls the choice undocumented.

steps.t: Trace for an unrelated folder that starts with the same letters finds {{matched_n}}
steps.d: A pattern such as hooks/** is cut to the prefix hooks, and any path starting with those letters counts, so a folder named hooksmith inherits every hooks decision.

steps.t: Rejected records are listed as governing too, marked only by their status
do: a rejected record is printed beside a proposed one, its status in brackets

steps.t: The reader either skips a real decision or re-reads unrelated ones
do: pass trace a path relative to the repository root, with no leading ./

scenarios.title: What if a record only named the winner?

steps.t: A record names one option and no assumption
Months later the session code is rewritten
Verify has nothing to run, and nobody can say whether the reason still holds

scenarios.title: Fix: lint refuses a conclusion dressed as a decision

steps.t: Lint refuses a record with one option: it is not a decision
It also refuses no assumptions, and an assumption with no revisit trigger
Verify lists a placeholder check as unverifiable instead of passing it quietly
steps.d: Verify still exits clean on a skip, so lint, not verify, is the gate that keeps empty checks out. And a weak check that always succeeds passes both.
do: SKIP on A1: no verify command, unverifiable

options.label: Each assumption carries its own check command; drift compares governed files since the record's commit
pros: A stale assumption fails a command, not someone's memory
Plain files, git and bash: nothing to host, same result every run
cons: Drift is path-level and noisy: in this repo today it flags {{attention_n}} of {{adr_n}} records
A weak check passes, and an unknown commit reads as no drift

options.label: Plain written decision records with no checks
cons: Cannot be traced from a file

options.label: Have an agent re-judge every decision against the code on each change
pros: Could notice a change that contradicts a decision, not just that files moved
cons: Costs a model run per decision per change
A different answer on each run, so it cannot gate CI

decision.deciding_factor: A check that runs the same way every time and costs nothing is one that actually gets run, before shipping and in CI.
decision.revisit_when: Drift fires on so many records that people stop reading it, or a missed drift ships a broken assumption.
decision.source: skills/decision-records/SKILL.md rules 2, 3 and 6, and its honest limitations; SOURCE: original

checks.q: The session file now imports a token library, but nothing is committed. Will drift notice?
checks.answer: No: drift diffs from the record's commit to the last commit. Verify already failed, because it runs the assumption's own check against the files as they are.

checks.q: The record's commit does not exist in this clone. What does drift print?
checks.answer: That nothing needs attention: the failed diff's exit status is ignored and its empty output reads as no changes.

checks.q: A record names one option and no assumptions. Does lint pass it?
checks.answer: No: one option is not a decision, and a record with no assumptions has nothing that could later be falsified.

notes.sh: Runs a command in the repository root and returns its exit status, output and error text.
notes.load_all: Reads every ADR file under the decisions folder and its shards; a missing or invalid meta block becomes an error entry, not a skip.
notes.next_id: The next ADR number: the highest one in the folder and its shards, plus one, padded.
notes.cmd_new: The new command: writes a numbered record from the template with the current commit and the given patterns and tags, then rewrites the index; a dry run prints the diff.
notes.cmd_index: The index command: rewrites the decisions table from every record's meta block, and lists malformed records separately.
notes.cmd_verify: The verify command: runs each live record's assumption checks in bash; a placeholder is a visible skip, a failure prints its revisit trigger.
notes.cmd_trace: The trace command: lists records whose affects patterns match the path, by glob or by text prefix, with each assumption's claim.
notes.cmd_check: For CI: lint, then index, then drift, failing if any of them fails.
